300.t: Buddy Petit joins Humphrey's band from Mandeville
300.s: Humphrey recalls Petit leaving Mandeville to join his band with Lee Collins for about two months around 1926, and names the personnel.
300.q: Well, I suppose it must have been just about 1926. And we had a gig over in Mandeville every other Saturday night. In the hotel. Buddy was stationed over there with another man. And it looks as though he had gotten tired of being over there, kind of lonesome, just working on weekends. So he decided…

300.t: Personnel of Buddy Petit's own band
300.s: Humphrey lists the members of Petit's six-piece band, the most popular jazz band of the time.
300.q: Buddy Manning on the band. Zeb, Ezeb Lenoris and Kleines. And, uh, Simon Maruero on bass violin. He had a six-piece band. Well, in case of him, he'd use the piano, well, he'd use what we call it, Tink. Xavier Batiste's piano. Yeah.

771.t: Bolden's band, Dusen and the Eagle Band
771.s: He tells how Bolden blew across the park to Lincoln Park, lists Bolden's sidemen, and how Dusen took over as the Eagle Band, which he joined on violin.
771.q: Well, a fella by the name of Edwild Clemmen, at that time. And then, later on, Bunk went with the Eagle Band, too. Now, the funny thing about Bunk, when he was with us downtown, the Superior Band, he didn't drink, he didn't have no bad habits at all. And when he went uptown with the Eagle Band,…

768.t: New Orleans musicians in Chicago: Perez, Tio, Dixon
768.s: Many New Orleans players were in Chicago; she recalls Manuel Perez and Tio at the Deluxe and a drummer and banjoist with Franz Jackson.
768.q: that No he came and played just a oh no I he may have been here earlier I understand that band was here in 1914 or something.

430.t: Young Olympia Band: Buddy Petit, Mac Lacey and Barbarin joining
430.s: Members of the Young Olympia band and how drummers followed one another until Barbarin joined.
430.q: That's, that's, that's many years back. Gee whiz. Um. Now they had some very good bands. I mean, uh, came behind this band like, uh, the Yama Lipi Band. Well, that band was terrific. It was in there. Yeah, that band was really a mess of me. They, they, they was better than those bands. Well, I got,…

258.t: Drumming in Buddy Petit's band and singing Tight Like That
258.s: He played about three weeks in Buddy Petit's band on Franklin Street with George Washington, Walter Decou and Big Eye Louis, and sang Tight Like That.
258.ch: Learning drums and trombone, New Orleans
258.q: Right. Right. Well, I played drums in there with him for about three weeks. Who else was in the band looking at? Well, at that time I remember Buddy Pity, a Trombone player called George Washington, was in the band then. He had a piano player in the band,

621.t: Who played in the Bolden band
621.s: Duhé and his visitors list members of the Bolden band they heard.
621.q: Brock. Brock, the Brock guitar. Willa Warner. They had two clarinet, Willa Warner. They had two clarinet, Willa Warner. They had two clarinet, yeah. And Willa Warner, yeah. Jimmy Johnson on the drums. Jimmy Johnson, that's a part of one of the drums. Henry Zeno on the drums. That's that thing,…

903.s: He played with the Excelsior brass band and jazz band, and remembers Wooden Joe as a powerful trumpet player.
903.q: Yeah, Excelsior, yeah. I played with a lot of them old fellas in the Excelsior brass band, Excelsior's jazz band too. I played with all of them, every band in town.

873.t: The French brothers and the French and White band
873.s: Morris, Bob and Johnny French had their own band called French and White.
873.q: Yeah. They had a band too. They had a band the same. Well, they left to Edward. They had a band too. They called it the French and White.

876.t: Superior band, shifting personnel and Big Eye Louis
876.s: Names of Superior band players, how musicians moved between bands, and Big Eye Louis's clarinet playing and reading ability versus George Baquet.
876.q: He was playing bass with the Superior. And Willie Santiago, I think Joe Brooks, Joe Brooks was playing with Olympia, too.

8.t: The Imperial Band lineup and Big Eye Louis
8.s: Members of the Imperial band behind Manuel Perez, including Jimmy Brown, Buddy Johnson's brother and violinist Peter Bocage, then clarinetist Big Eye Louis.
8.ch: Bands and musicians around New Orleans
8.q: Yanks, brother. Yanks, yeah. Buddy Johnson's brother. Yeah. Yeah. And, uh... Willie San Diego, who was sleepy. Yeah. He was on the guitar. And, uh... He was on the drums at that time. And, you know, uh... I think, uh... I forgot who was on the drums. I can't think of his name. I know it. I can't…

571.t: Buddy Petit's band and its players
571.s: Lewis names musicians who played with Buddy Petit's band and others around it.
571.q: Chris... Chris... Chris on out here. As he went along with it. That band that was in that band before... Uh, by John and Buddy Petit's band. Uh... There were a few of them done in Reed. There were a few of them bumped with by John and Buddy Petit's band. And, uh, the reason. And, uh... The... The…

53.t: Bolden-era musicians and the Johnson brothers of Algiers
53.s: Mary and Allen try to name Bolden's band members, Frankie Dusen and others. They recall Buddy and Yank Johnson of Algiers, schoolmates of Mary.
53.q: Yes, yes. He was of a dark complex with straight hair. Frankie Doosan. He came from Algiers too, Professor. Why, I know the whole family. I'm trying to think of all of them. But I just can't think it's been so long in no years. Frankie Doosan.

138.t: Other bands across the river, Minetta, Divergis
138.s: Russell asks about Johnny Fisher, a Minetta band and Al Divergis; Laine knows little. Laine adds that whenever music was needed, people came to him.
138.q: Johnny Fisher played there not much. No. I don't know. I thought he would. No, I don't. Outside of Johnny Fisher. No. I don't.

293.s: Names violinists and others he heard, including Paul Dominguez, Piron, Chris Kelly, Freddie Washington and Simeon, and says many are now dead.
293.q: Oh yeah, no of my folks never played but there's a lot of fellas like Paul Dominguez. Was he playing violin? Violin, he was playing in them days. And Piron, he was playing in those days. And I just can't call a lot of those guys names, you know what I mean? I forgot a lot of them. Oh sure. And…

781.t: Playing guitar in Buddy Petit's band around 1918
781.s: In Buddy Petit's band around 1918 were George Washington, drummer Charny, a bass player and a clarinettist.
781.q: Me and George Washington. And who else was with me and Buddy George Washington. Oh, and this Les Short-Jumma, I can't call his name. And I think Drags was playing Pace, if I'm not mistaken. And who the Clannette played, I can't recall his name now, he passed on.

832.t: Seven years with Amos Riley, then Buddy Petit's band
832.s: Foster says he was with Amos Riley about seven years until Riley died, then joined Buddy Petit's band on drums, and names its members Chester Zardis, Manuel Gabriel, Louis Keppard and Isidore Fritz.
832.q: Buddy died. I'm not. Let me see. No, not 23. No, indeed. Buddy died, 32. That's when Buddy died in 32 July the 4th. Buddy B. T. I played Buddy B. T.'s band after Amos Rowley, you see. Oh, I see. I played Amos Rowley's band regularly. And then Amos died.

997.t: Kid Rena band members and other clarinettists
997.s: He names men in Rena's band, including T-Boy and Zeb, and clarinettists George Abbott and Joe Watson who played by ear.
997.q: No, T-Boy's a bass player. They got T-Boy Rene and me play trumpet too, you know. Yeah, then they got a T-Boy, I believe he was playing bands with Kid Rene too.

106.s: Briggs recalls the former Original Dixieland Jazz Band trombonist Emile Christian as a regular at the Paris Flea Pit and well liked, who vanished at the start of the war.
106.q: Yes, sure. I know him from Paris, and Emile was a regular guy, 'cause he was always with us. We were at the "Flea Pit," as I told you about.

641.t: Why Toots Johnson's band was the one remembered
641.s: Joe says Toots always had the best men, such as Buddy Petit.
641.ch: Instruments, first jobs and the regional scene
641.q: Well, Toots Johnson always had the best men. Like I said, Toots Johnson had guys like Buddy Petit, and I think just before Guy Kelly left Baton Rouge he played with Toots Johnson.
